title: Moon and star motif
subtitle: A crescent moon with a five-pointed star companion, 10 cm
excerpt: The moon and star motif combines a crescent moon worked as a curved flat applique in silver-grey with a small five-pointed star worked separately and sewn beside it. At 10 cm the pair reads clearly at distance and works as a nursery wall decoration, celestial-theme cushion applique, and gift wrapping embellishment.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from crescent and star applique construction. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 7 (1892), celestial motif chapter (Internet Archive).

chartDefinition.title: Moon and star motif
chartDefinition.caption: Moon: curved flat strip in dc rows, narrowing at each end and curving with gentle increases/decreases. Star: five treble cluster spokes from magic ring with ch-3 tips.

glossaryTerms.definition: Multiple trebles worked into the same space and drawn together at the top. The star has five treble cluster spokes from its magic ring centre.

content.text: The crescent moon is worked as a tapered flat strip: a wide centre row that narrows toward each horn tip. The curvature comes from working more stitches on the outer edge than the inner edge in each row — a simple bias effect that bends the strip into a crescent. The star is a compact five-
treble cluster
piece from a magic ring, worked in gold or yellow, then sewn beside the moon.

The crescent does not need stiffening — the bias tension from the dc rows holds the curve. If the curl is stronger than desired, block the inner edge longer than the outer edge over a curved foam surface.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of silver-grey DK cotton for the moon, 3 g of gold or yellow for the star. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
The crescent moon measures 8 cm tall. The companion star measures 4 cm across. Combined motif spans 10 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc), dc2tog — UK; US "single crochet / sc2tog".
treble cluster (3tr-cl) — for the star spokes.
Pattern
Crescent moon — silver-grey

Ch 20. Dc in 2nd ch from hook and across. (18 dc.) Turn. Row 2: Ch 1. Dc2tog. Dc to last 2. Dc2tog on the inner (concave) edge only — leave the outer (convex) edge as is. Turn. Repeat rows 3 to 5 in the same way, decreasing only at the inner edge by 1 dc each row, reaching 14 dc at the widest section. Rows 6 to 8: Decrease on both edges to begin tapering both horns simultaneously. Row 9: Continue tapering the upper horn to 3 dc. Fasten off. Re-join yarn to the lower horn and taper symmetrically to 3 dc. Fasten off.
Companion star — gold

Form a magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Work 2 more tr, draw together (first 3tr-cl). *Ch 2. 3tr-cl.* Repeat 3 more times. Ch 2. Sl st to top of first cluster. (5 clusters.) Tips: *Sl st into ch-2 sp. Ch 3. Dc in 2nd ch (tip). Ch 2. Sl st back.* Repeat for all 5 spaces. Fasten off with 20 cm tail.
Assembly
Sew the star to the concave side of the crescent, positioning it in the upper curve between the two horns.

definition.title: Moon and star motif
definition.caption: Crescent: 9-row dc strip, decreasing on inner edge only in rows 2-5, both edges in rows 6-9 to taper the two horns. Star: 5 treble clusters from magic ring with ch-3 tips.

content.text: Finishing
Weave in all ends. Sew the assembled moon and star onto the base fabric, or attach a hanging cord for use as an ornament.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Re-curve the crescent by pressing lightly with a damp cloth into the crescent shape while damp.
What to try next

The star wreath (crochet-themed-star-wreath) scales the star to a full 10 cm and arranges five in a ring. The basic heart (crochet-themed-heart-basic) uses the same flat-strip construction logic applied to a different shape.
